asr_text: After that, an index showing world market prices fell by 25 percent over seven months. The USDA links this drop to extra supplies becoming easier to get. But in the United States, the coffee part of the consumer price index was still higher than in the same month a year earlier. Wait a minute, that doesn't add up. You might want to say that. But one is a world market index and the other is the U.S. consumer price index. One shows a drop over seven months, while the other compares prices with the year earlier. They are on different stages and run on different clocks. If you pour the numbers into the same cup, the story gets muddled. And price tags follow their own schedule. Market experts and others interviewed by Reuters estimated that it takes around nine months or longer for green bean prices to show up in store prices. If market prices are a breaking news alert, price tags are patient letters.
